svg.text: 06 · The model plane and fairness — one choke point for the most expensive resource
llm.Gateway.Complete() is the only code path to a provider. It reserves quota before the call, retries with full jitter, settles against real usage, and never fails a run for a provider outage.
called by a worker's step(); returns a Response or an error the worker turns into a requeue
weighted max-min fairness = one token bucket per tenant + one shared spare bucket
req = {model, system, messages (Rebuild), tools: SchemasFor(def.Tools), max_tokens}
est = EstimateTokens(req) // character-count heuristic over system+messages+tools, + output
ok=false → return ErrQuotaUnavailable immediately — the worker requeues the run with wake_at = now+2 s
the worker's goroutine is free within microseconds; it leases some other tenant's run
resp, err = primary.Complete(ctx, req) (per-call ctx timeout)
not retryable (4xx other than 429) → break with the error
attempt == 3 and fallback configured and retryable → try fallback provider instead
backoff = 250 ms × 2^(attempt−1); sleep = rand(0, backoff) ← FULL jitter
(AWS 'Exponential Backoff And Jitter': full jitter minimises retry collisions
across 500 agents hitting the same 429 at the same second)
over-estimate → tokens refunded to the tenant's bucket · under-estimate → charged, may go negative
Reservation.settled guards double settlement; a failed call settles with 0 (full refund)
metrics.ModelCall(tenant, model, in, out, costUSD) — cost from the price table in code
Response{content, tool_calls, stop_reason, tokens, cost} → the worker writes MODEL_RESPONSE
after 3 failures → error to the worker
the worker does NOT fail the run: requeue with wake_at = now+10 s, status_reason 'model provider unavailable'
durability means an outage is a delay, not a loss; the event log has no partial step
budget check happens BEFORE the call, so a retry storm can never overspend a run
take(n) / give(n) · tokens may go NEGATIVE (deficit)
starts EMPTY: capacity is spare only
once it has actually gone unused
any tenant may borrow from it after its own bucket
b = buckets[tenant]; unknown tenant → false (fail closed)
if b.tokens − need ≥ floor: b.tokens −= need → ok
backpressure = NOT scheduling, never a blocked worker
a tenant in deficit waits until refill catches up
SpareTokens() for the shared pool gauge
Why max-min with weights, and not a global bucket or fixed quotas
a global bucket lets one tenant's 300-agent burst starve everyone (first come, first served) · fixed quotas waste idle capacity
weighted max-min: every tenant is GUARANTEED its share and may BORROW what others leave idle; guarantees always sum to the provider rate
error class from the provider adapter
≤3 attempts, full-jitter backoff, fallback on the last; then requeue +10
a run's first step waits out the outage; nothing is lost, nothing is
duplicated (no side effect in a model call)
Reserve() false · Eligible() omits the tenant
run requeued +2 s or simply not leased; workers serve other tenants
interactive work can dip into the 20 % reserve; batch cannot — batch latency
refund or charge; deficits allowed so the tenant self-corrects next
a huge under-estimate lets one call overshoot its share once — bounded by
buckets rebuilt from tenants table on start; each replica admits
N replicas ⇒ up to N× over-admission — the documented reason Redis is in the
a misconfigured tenant gets NO model access rather than unlimited access
